background_notes.fact: For x>=1 and p>=1, x^(-p)<=x^(-1). For gamma>0, x->x^gamma is increasing on positive reals and (a^(1/gamma))^gamma=a for a>0. Thus the tail bound in S001 holds, and the threshold in S003 satisfies Csmooth*tau0^gamma<=1/4.

background_notes.justification: On positive reals use x^r=exp(r log x). For x>=1, log x>=0 gives -p log x<=-log x. The strict monotonicity of log and exp gives the other monotonicity and power-composition identities. All bases used here are positive.

background_notes.fact: For T>0, d>0, L a positive integer and tau=T/L<=d/2, m=floor(d/tau) is an integer >=2 and d/2<=m*tau<=d. Splitting L steps into blocks of m steps and a possible remainder uses at most ceiling(2*T/d)+1 blocks. Truncating at any time in [0,T] preserves that bound and grid starts.

background_notes.justification: The Archimedean floor property gives d/tau-1<m<=d/tau, hence m*tau>d-tau>=d/2 and m*tau<=d. Each completed full block consumes at least d/2 time, so there are at most 2*T/d full blocks, plus at most one shorter block. Stopping inside a block only shortens that last block.

background_notes.fact: For every real t, S_t is a linear isometry on each H^s, with inverse S_(-t), and is strongly continuous there. Consequently continuous u:[0,T]->H^gamma gives continuous v(t)=S_(-t)u(t) in L2 when gamma>0, and ||S_(-t)(u-u^n)||_2=||u-u^n||_2.

background_notes.justification: The multiplier has modulus one and its inverse is obtained by changing t to -t, proving isometry and the inverse identity directly in the Fourier norm. Strong continuity holds on finite Fourier sums by continuity of each scalar exponential; approximate an arbitrary element by such a sum, bounding each of the two tail terms by isometry. Finally split S_(-t)u(t)-S_(-s)u(s) into the isometric image of u(t)-u(s) and the group difference applied to the fixed u(s). This proves the continuity used in S003 and the norm equality used in S004.

background_notes.fact: A continuous L2-valued error e on [0,T] with e(0)=0, if its norm ever reaches or exceeds one, has a first t*>0 with ||e(t*)||_2=1 and ||e(t)||_2<=1 for 0<=t<=t*. Thus every block or truncated block before t* satisfies the bootstrap condition.

background_notes.justification: The reverse triangle inequality makes t->||e(t)||_2 continuous. The intermediate value theorem makes the level-one set nonempty whenever the norm is at least one somewhere. This level set is closed in the compact interval, so it has a smallest element t*>0. Any earlier norm greater than one would force an earlier level-one point by the intermediate value theorem. The contradiction at t* in S003 therefore removes the bootstrap assumption.
